verbs.summary: commit/push nag (bare); restic family + git-bundle net: init|status|run|drill|bundle
verbs.usage: plainkeep backup [status | run [--target local|cloud] --yes | drill --yes | bundle [--dry-run] | init --yes]
verbs.hints: Bare `plainkeep backup` is the UNCHANGED read-only commit/push nag (exit 1 = at risk; never pushes for you). Subcommands add the restic durability floor (auto-detected; degrades with an install hint): init (human-run once, --yes, writes .backup/config.json with op:// REFERENCES + renders the launchd plist), status (snapshot age per target, exit 1 if stale >48h or unconfigured), run [--target local|cloud] (cloud is --yes ALWAYS; the scheduled cloud push runs from launchd DIRECTLY with an append-only B2 key, outside this verb), drill (--yes; restore latest snapshot to tmp and diff), bundle (git bundle --all of ~/plainkeep + every ~/work repo into ~/files/backups/bundles/ with retention). Common mistake: expecting bare backup to run restic — it only nags; use `plainkeep backup run`.

verbs.hints: Save a URL as a wiki bookmark note (title fetched best-effort). Body text is extracted via trafilatura when installed (optional dep; pip install trafilatura), else a crude zero-dependency tag-strip. --archive additionally snapshots the fetched page HTML into ~/files/bookmarks/ against link-rot (skipped if the page wasn't reachable). Any http(s) URL is accepted as a generic link/article — a tweet or video URL is saved the same way, there is no special x.com/YouTube parsing (see `plainkeep files extract` for transcript extraction of an already-ingested media file). Common mistake: --archive without a reachable page — the HTML snapshot is skipped.

Same brain as zsh tab-completion (`plainkeep __complete`), derived live from each verb's cmd.json actions[]/args (no hardcoded tables). Use --json for the machine rows; without it, one `value  description` per line. Common mistake: passing the word being completed — pass only the words BEFORE it (e.g. `plainkeep complete task move` lists statuses).

verbs.hints: Generate a description + keywords for one note (source: its .extract.md if it has one, else its own body) and write them to the note's frontmatter — never to the .extract.md, which --reextract rewrites. Idempotent via an enrich_key: hash of (model, text); a plain re-run on unchanged text is a no-op, --reenrich forces. --all sweeps every note lacking a current key, sequentially, under one warm model load. Auto-wired (best-effort) into `files extract` and `bookmark` unless PLAINKEEP_ENRICH=off. Common mistake: expecting meta on the .extract.md — it lives on the shadow/primary note.

verbs.summary: binary assets: ingest [<path>] [--client|--project|--area <slug>|--research] [--extract] | extract <slug> | distill <slug> | link <file> <hub> | list | open <slug>
verbs.usage: plainkeep files ingest [<path>] [--client|--project|--area <slug> | --research] [--extract] | extract <slug> [--reextract] [--heavy] [--lang <x>] [--diarize] [--describe] | distill <slug> | link <file> <hub> | list [--hub <slug>] | open <slug>
verbs.hints: The binary-assets plane: ingest routes a file into ~/files + writes a wiki shadow note; extract emits a SIBLING derived note wiki/files/<slug>.extract.md (type extract|transcript, derived_from/source_sha256/tool) from the source bytes via an auto-detected media tier: pdf -> markdown, audio/video/URL -> transcript, image -> OCR/VLM description, txt/md -> plain text. Each tier is an optional dep (pymupdf4llm/docling, mlx-whisper/faster-whisper/parakeet-mlx, yt-dlp, ocrmac/tesseract) that degrades to a one-line install hint instead of crashing; a URL source needs a shadow note whose path: is already the URL (no ingest <url> support yet). distill compiles that extract into 1-N author:agent/status:draft concept notes in wiki/notes/ (typed JSON payload with an agent, heading-outline fallback without; promote via `plainkeep triage drafts`). Same-bytes+same-tool re-run is a no-op; --reextract forces. Common mistake: expecting the binary in git — only the plaintext shadow + extract notes are tracked; and expecting a transcript without the tier's dep installed (it degrades with an install hint).

verbs.usage: plainkeep models list | status | stop [--all] [<model>] | pull [--stage <s>|--all] --yes | test <stage> [--model <m>] [--input <file>] --yes
reads: PLAINKEEP_OCR / PLAINKEEP_VLM / PLAINKEEP_ENRICH_MODEL / PLAINKEEP_EMBED_MODEL / PLAINKEEP_RERANK_MODEL env
writes: ollama's local model store (pull only; outside ~/plainkeep)

A model (PLAINKEEP_AGENT) only RANKS confidences; with none, heuristics. review appends accept/reject/defer status lines (audit ledger, latest wins) and shows the exact diff each op would produce. apply (needs --yes, NEVER schedulable; apply --dry-run previews the exact replay and writes nothing) deterministically replays APPROVED ops only, one commit per op, with an edit budget (20 ops / 300 lines, flags may only lower it) and protected paths (conventions/index/hubs/pinned) review-only; retitle/propose_merge/deletions never auto-apply. --safe-only applies only the four additive primitives above 0.8. Common mistake: expecting apply to run a model (it never does) or to touch a protected path.

verbs.summary: layered installer dashboard and idempotent setup runner
reads: Python package index / configured pip indexes (external, confirm-gated)
Ollama daemon and model registry (external/local, confirm-gated)
template repo GitHub release assets via the gh CLI (plainkeep-ui binary, confirm-gated)
verbs.hints: Bare `plainkeep setup` is a read-only layered dashboard. `plainkeep setup <layer>` advances one layer idempotently. `plainkeep setup --wizard` is a guided, interactive first-run: one skippable prompt per layer with safe defaults (skeleton and the terminal UI on; search/models/automation off), interactive-only (needs a tty; not with --json/--dry-run — those exit 2 pointing at `plainkeep setup --all --yes` / `plainkeep setup --json`). Search and model layers can install Python packages and pull Ollama models into external stores, and the ui layer downloads the compiled plainkeep-ui binary (sha256-verified, via the authenticated gh CLI) into .local/bin, so they require `--yes`; backups is a human handoff and is never included in `--all`. `--dry-run` previews any advance (single layer or `--all`) without installing/writing and needs no `--yes`.

verbs.summary: capability-URL share: publish a note (or tag collection) as one unguessable link; browser gets HTML, <url>.md is raw markdown for agents
verbs.usage: plainkeep share <slug> [--expires 7d] [--gist] [--dry-run|--yes] | collection <tag> | list | pull <url> | revoke <id> --yes | init
verbs.hints: Share a note or `collection <tag>` as ONE self-contained OPSX bundle (raw markdown + rendered HTML), published PLAINTEXT to a Cloudflare Worker+KV under a 24-char unguessable token (~124 bits) -- no encryption, no key. Secrecy = link secrecy + TTL, same trust model as a secret gist; the worker can technically read published content (accepted tradeoff, see ADR-008). ONE link for everyone: the bare URL renders HTML in a browser; append `.md` (or paste the printed `agents:` line) and any chat/coding agent's fetch tool gets raw wiki markdown -- content negotiation also serves markdown to non-browser Accept headers on the bare URL. `plainkeep share pull <url>` fetches + unpacks the same markdown locally. Legacy encrypted links from the old zero-knowledge model return 410 -- re-publish. Transmitting subactions (share/collection/revoke) self-gate --yes -> EXIT_CONFIRM(3) because a PUT is a transmission; `list` and `pull` are free reads. `--dry-run` renders locally and stops before the PUT. `--gist` = secret gist fallback (same trust model, hosted by GitHub). `plainkeep share init` deploys the worker and provisions the `X-Publish-Token` (`--yes` runs `wrangler deploy` + `wrangler secret put PUBLISH_TOKEN`). Common mistake: expecting it to send the link — output is a DRAFT link, the human sends it.

Everything fails closed: unknown schema, malformed JSON, or a duplicate id/name/path refuses with the file named. NOTE: this does not yet change how a root is DISCOVERED (Task 1b) — `vault status` reports what today's rules select.

args.help: the note type (its template + folder); the `note-type` provider lists the live registry (built-ins + templates/wiki/types.json)

args.name: name
args.help: the note title (slugified for the filename)

actions.name: backlinks
actions.summary: notes that link to this one

actions.name: stale
actions.summary: notes not updated in N+ days

actions.name: orphans
actions.summary: type-note notes with no inbound links

actions.name: canvas
actions.summary: write a JSON Canvas over the wikilink graph around a hub or tag

args.name: target
args.help: a hub note slug, or a #tag (all tagged notes)

args.name: --depth
args.help: hops out from the hub (hub mode only)

args.name: --stdout
args.help: print the canvas JSON instead of writing wiki/canvas/<slug>.canvas

actions.name: list
actions.summary: note counts by type (the default action)
